sources.citation: Ethnologue, Kamantan [kci] page (2019 capture via the Internet Archive).
sources.note: Alternate names Angan, Kamanton; Kaduna State, Kachia LGA; population 10,000 (Barrett 1982); no typology line, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2018. Nominal affixes and number marking in the Plateau languages of Central Nigeria. In John R. Watters (ed.), East Benue-Congo: Nouns, pronouns, and verbs (Niger-Congo Comparative Studies 1), 107-172. Berlin: Language Science Press. doi:10.5281/zenodo.1314325.
sources.note: Only nominal morphology: Table 3 'Gyongic: Gyong (=Kagoma), Kamanton -- Very restricted alternating prefixes, palatalisation, concord; Similar to Gyong (Hagen 1988)'; sec. 2.3.6: 'Neither language is well-known but there is a description of Gyong which includes information on noun-classes (Hagen 1988). According to this, Gyong marks plurals with prefix alternation, palatalisation alternation and tone.' Tone-marked Gyong forms are cited; nothing on Angan/Kamanton phonology, tone system or stress.

sources.citation: Dabet, Julius (transcriber). 2018. Wordlist: Kamantan (Anghan) [kci]. Nigerian Word List (Hausa version), 348 items, collected 16 Mar 2018 at Lenak Anghan, Zangon Kataf LGA, Kaduna State. Jos: SIL Nigeria. SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 83623 (draft). 22 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Handwritten field wordlist (IPA with tone diacritics, sg/pl columns); no prose at all, no statement on stress or accent.

sources.citation: Usman, Daniel P. 2015 (alphabet revised 2020). Gbangche Buo Zhayhian Anghan [community Nghian (Anghan) alphabet and primer]. Internal publication, Anghan community, Fadan Kamantan; excerpted as 'Nghian Language: Introduction to Nghian Language & Writtings', Anghan People blog, 31 October 2021.
sources.note: Amateur community orthography: five vowels a e i o u with example words, 'long vowel' written with apostrophe (a'), consonant inventory presented through digraphs gh, jh, kh, kp, sh, yh, zh ('z, s, j, q, g, k, y are missing ordinarily'), letter names, numerals 1-30 (base-10 with khuob '10', shuoyhual '20'), place/food/animal/greeting wordlists. Tone is not marked and never discussed (only a vague remark that the added 'h' 'carries a sound.. provides native sounds or tunes'); nothing on stress or accent.
sources.venue: Gbangche Buo Zhayhian Anghan [community Nghian (Anghan) alphabet and primer]

sources.citation: Gunn, Harold D. 1956. Pagan peoples of the central area of Northern Nigeria (Ethnographic Survey of Africa, Western Africa XII). London: International African Institute. Section 'Kamantan' (read in the Human Relations Area Files FF38 'Katab' file, processed 1960, together with the file's excerpts of Meek 1931 Tribal Studies in Northern Nigeria vol. II; microfiche scanned to archive.org 2026, item micro_IA41160219_0013).
sources.note: No phonology content for Kamantan: nomenclature, population, location, exogamous sections, chiefship, traditions of origin ('Angan believe themselves to be Kagoro emigrants'; 'linguistic evidence seems to support Reynolds'), bibliography pointer to Meek's unpublished 'Kamantan tribe, Anthropological notes on' (Secretariat, Northern Provinces). The FF38 file contains no Kamantan vocabulary.
